diagnostic_evidence.quote: The entropy variables are defined as the partial derivative of the entropy function $\mathbb{E}$ with respect to the conservative variables $(h,hu_m,h\bB{\alpha})$.
which follows directly as the entropy variables assume a constant value for the lake-at-rest conditions \eqref{eq:lake_at_rest}.

issues.failure_explanation: After augmenting the conservative state by $b$, the last component of the gradient of the stated energy is $\partial_b\mathbb E=gh$, not $b$. Thus the appended vector is not an entropy-variable vector under the paper's own definition. Moreover, at lake at rest its appended component $b$ need not be constant, so the quoted step in the well-balancedness proof is false. The dissipation can still vanish because its last row and column are zero, but that different argument is not the one given.

failure_location.quote: To this end, we add the bottom topography to both vectors of conservative variables $\bB{u} = (h,hu_m,h\alpha_1,h\alpha_2,\dots,h\alpha_N,b)^{\rm T}\in \mathbb{R}^{N+3}$ as well as entropy variables $\bB{w} = (w_1,w_2,\dots,w_{N+2},b)^{\rm T} \in \mathbb{R}^{N+3}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Call the appended vector an auxiliary multiplier rather than the gradient of the augmented entropy, and repair the well-balancedness proof by observing that the first $N+2$ components are constant at lake at rest while the zero final row and column of $\mbf Q_{\tt ES}$ annihilate the nonconstant $b$ component.
issues.overall_effect: The interpretation of the augmented multiplier as entropy variables is false, and the stated justification of the interface-dissipation cancellation in the well-balancedness lemma is invalid as written.
issues.title: The augmented vector is not the gradient of the stated entropy
issues.why_classification: A short local reinterpretation and proof correction preserves the entropy inequality and well-balancedness guarantee without changing the scheme.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In this example, the friction is modelled via the Newtonian slip law given by the function $\mbf{S}=\mbf{S}_{\rm Ns}$ \eqref{eq:friction:Nslip}, which corresponds to the source term in \eqref{sys:SWME:vectorial}.
The corresponding source term related to the chosen manufactured solution is then obtained by replacing $\bB{u}_{\rm ex}$ into the left-hand side of \eqref{sys:SWME:vectorial}

issues.failure_explanation: The numerical system is introduced with a nonzero source $\mbf S$, and several numerical examples require friction or manufactured sources, but both the displayed DGSEM and its entropy-stable version have zero right-hand sides and no source discretization is specified. Consequently, the written procedure does not approximate the nonhomogeneous problems used in those examples.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the appropriately weighted nodal source contribution to the semidiscrete equations and state how it is evaluated; for the friction sources, note that the pointwise entropy-dissipation calculation carries over under positive quadrature weights.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the algorithm only defines the homogeneous spatial discretization and cannot produce the claimed frictional or manufactured-source computations.
issues.title: The displayed DGSEM omits the source term of the modeled system
issues.why_classification: A standard local nodal source term completes the method and preserves the advertised spatial construction without requiring new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The right-hand side of the EC definition is the specialization of the preceding general formula for $\mbf D^-$. It uses only the minus state and is therefore not a definition of both $\mbf D^-_{\tt EC}$ and $\mbf D^+_{\tt EC}$. In particular, the plus fluctuation required at left interfaces is not correctly defined, and using the displayed expression for both signs violates the preceding path-conservation construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the two fluctuations separately: $\mbf D^-_{\tt EC}=\mbf f^{\tt EC}-\mbf f^-+\tfrac12\mbf B^-\jump{\bB u}$ and $\mbf D^+_{\tt EC}=\mbf f^+-\mbf f^{\tt EC}+\tfrac12\mbf B^+\jump{\bB u}$, consistently with the preceding formula.
issues.overall_effect: The entropy-conservative and entropy-stable DGSEM procedures are not fully or consistently defined at element interfaces, so their stated semidiscrete entropy guarantee does not follow for the algorithm literally displayed.
issues.title: The entropy-conservative fluctuation formula defines only the minus fluctuation
issues.why_classification: The required correction is local and uniquely determined by the already stated general fluctuation formula; it preserves all intended guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the unscaled coefficients are $\widetilde{A}_{ijk}\coloneqq A_{ijk}/(2i+1)$ and $\widetilde{B}_{ijk} \coloneqq B_{ijk}/(2i+1)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation \eqref{eq:condition} is an identity for the scaled coefficients. Substituting the definitions gives $B_{ijk}/(2i+1)+A_{kji}/(2k+1)+B_{kji}/(2k+1)=0$, hence $A_{kji}=-B_{kji}-\frac{2k+1}{2i+1}B_{ijk}$, not the stated unweighted sum when $i\ne k$. Thus the prescribed coefficient-generation procedure generally produces the wrong $A$ tensor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the scaling factors when reconstructing $A$, using $A_{kji}=-B_{kji}-\frac{2k+1}{2i+1}B_{ijk}$, and recompute or verify all numerical results that used the erroneous reconstruction.
issues.overall_effect: An implementation following the appendix solves a system with incorrect moment flux coefficients. The coefficient identity used by the entropy-conservative flux proof then need not hold, so the implemented SWME flux and the claimed numerical entropy conservation are unreliable, as are numerical results generated by that procedure.
issues.title: The proposed reconstruction of the unscaled tensor A from B drops scaling factors
issues.why_classification: Although the formula itself has a contained correction, the stated implementation may have used wrong model coefficients, requiring recomputation and revalidation of the numerical experiments and entropy behavior.
